notes: Read both targets and full context. Resolve labor laws, national jurisdiction and the unnamed current administration to source-bounded roles in 2016 without inventing a president's name. Preserve allegations about government action as source assertions, not independent legal findings; distinguish characterizations of intent and labor-law obsolescence from policy commitments.

claims.claim_text: Hard-working Americans are the greatest asset of the U.S. economy.

Support for employment growth as the first economic priority, guiding education, workforce development, welfare reform, regulatory reform and trade agreements that expand opportunities for U.S. workers.
Opposition to outdated U.S. labor laws that restrict workers' freedom and impose obsolete workplace rules.
The U.S. administration in office in 2016 and its officials at the National Labor Relations Board are characterized as determined to reverse workplace change.
The U.S. administration in office in 2016 and its National Labor Relations Board officials are attacking the franchise business-development model.
The franchise business-development model is essential to flexibility and creativity in the new economy.

The U.S. administration in office in 2016 and its National Labor Relations Board officials are using 1930s Fair Labor Standards Act provisions designed for manufacturing to deny employers and employees flexibility.
The U.S. administration in office in 2016 and its National Labor Relations Board officials have repealed union-transparency rules that allowed members to discover how their dues were used.
The U.S. administration in office in 2016 and its National Labor Relations Board officials have outlawed alternatives to unions even when workers favored those alternatives.
